title: AES SETKEY returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE to force software schedule for GCM H-subkey — defend this
description: Why correct: AES-GCM requires aes->rounds to be set for software H-subkey precomputation done inside wc_AesGcmSetKey. If SETKEY returned 0 (claimed), wolfSSL would skip the software key schedule and aes->rounds would be zero/garbage. The first GcmEncrypt call would fail with KEYUSAGE_E or silently use a wrong H-subkey. Returning CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE forces wolfSSL to run the software key schedule. The port's hardware cipher path (crypto2dev_cipher) checks devCtx first and uses the device regardless, so both the hardware key store and the software schedule coexist correctly. What a contributor might change: 'SETKEY should return 0 to avoid the software schedule overhead, and we can init rounds ourselves.' Do not do this — it creates a subtle KEYUSAGE_E failure that only appears with AES-GCM, not AES-CBC.
